row.description: 3GPP PLMN display notation uses a three-digit Mobile Country Code and a two- or three-digit Mobile Network Code separated by a literal hyphen, as in 310-260. A wrong generalization would remove the hyphen because database forms often concatenate MCC and MNC, thereby accepting an unformatted identifier where this presentation convention requires the separator.

neighbors.relationship: A subscriber number may be served by a PLMN but does not encode MCC-MNC in this hyphenated form.
An IMSI begins with MCC and MNC but continues with a subscriber identity and is not written as a standalone PLMN code.

row.description: RFC 3261 SIP URI syntax permits a repeated semicolon-prefixed URI-parameter section after the host, for example transport and user parameters. A wrong generalization would model only one parameter because examples often show a single suffix, rejecting valid URIs with multiple parameter sections.

neighbors.relationship: A tel URI identifies a telephone number and uses different parameter rules from a SIP URI.
A Contact header may contain a SIP URI but additionally has header-level display-name and parameter syntax.

row.description: ITU-T E.164 international-number notation uses a leading plus sign followed by up to 15 digits. Samples from one national numbering plan can appear to have a fixed width, but E.164 is variable-width across country codes and national significant numbers. A wrong generalization would hard-code the apparent sample length, such as 11 digits, and reject valid shorter or longer international numbers.

neighbors.relationship: A national significant number is interpreted within a numbering plan and normally omits the E.164 plus form.
An IMSI is a mobile subscriber identity that can begin with country and network codes but is not an E.164 dialable number.

row.description: The U.S. Standard Form 424 naming convention may append an optional parenthesized revision month and year, such as SF-424 (Rev. 12/2022).

neighbors.distinction: Identifies an information-collection approval, commonly in a 1234-5678 pattern.
Names a related budget-information form rather than a revision of SF-424.

row.wrong_generalization: Requiring a revision mark because every sampled PDF happens to show one would reject valid base form labels; allowing arbitrary parenthetical prose would lose the controlled revision-date structure.

row.convention: HGVS sequence-variant nomenclature for cis-listed cDNA substitutions

uses p. amino-acid notation

row.wrong_generalization: Flattening the bracketed expression into an unrestricted delimiter-separated string loses the allele grouping and incorrectly permits commas, dangling separators, or an unbracketed multi-variant list.

row.description: ISBN-13 is the book-identification convention defined by ISO 2108. This profile uses the visible 3-1-4-4-1 hyphenation layout. A wrong generalization would treat hyphens as optional decoration or accept any 13-digit number without validating the ISBN-13 check digit and registration-group structure.

neighbors.distinction: ISSN identifies serial publications and has eight digits rather than the ISBN-13 book identifier layout.

row.description: PDF print and export dialogs conventionally express selected page intervals as comma-separated inclusive ranges, for example 1-3,5-7. A wrong generalization would treat the field as unrestricted prose, allow a bare page number when this range-only profile is expected, or accept typographic dashes that a machine parser does not recognize as range separators.

neighbors.distinction: A single page reference names one page, while this profile requires explicit start-end range sections.
A bookmark destination is a navigational target rather than a print-selection interval list.

row.description: A classic PDF cross-reference-table entry stores its byte offset as a zero-padded decimal field with exactly ten digits before the generation-number field. The apparent fixed width in samples is normative for the classic xref-table syntax, not evidence that offsets are ordinary variable-width integers. A wrong generalization would strip leading zeros or accept shorter offsets without padding.

neighbors.distinction: The generation number is a bounded object-version counter, while this field is a byte position in the PDF file.
A stream length is ordinarily represented as an integer object and is not constrained to the classic xref ten-character field width.

row.description: The commercial AWS partition convention for naming an S3 bucket resource is arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name. S3 bucket ARNs deliberately leave the region and account components empty.

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to require every AWS ARN to contain nonempty region and account fields. S3 bucket ARNs use the same colon-separated ARN shape but intentionally leave both fields blank.

row.description: An API Gateway route method is an IANA-registered HTTP method token, such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, CONNECT, or TRACE.

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to accept any uppercase alphabetic token as an HTTP method. Route configuration should use the IANA HTTP-method vocabulary rather than treating arbitrary verbs as valid methods.

row.description: S3 object keys are flat strings, but console and tooling conventions use slash-terminated repeated segments as a folder-style prefix, for example logs/2025/.

row.description: Course learning outcomes are often tagged as CLO-1, CLO-2, and so on; catalog and accreditation exports may serialize multiple tags as a semicolon-delimited list. row.description: Route manifest codes consist of two uppercase route letters and may carry an X inspection suffix. The observed examples all omit that suffix.

Maven commonly writes a dependency coordinate as groupId:artifactId. The literal colon separates two identifiers. A wrong generalization would treat any punctuation-separated pair as equivalent, accepting slash-separated package paths or replacing the colon with a dot.

neighbors.relationship: Often extends this form with a version, as group:artifact:version.
Uses an optional @scope/name structure instead of a colon separator.

row.description: RFC 1945 HTTP/1.0 defines the closed request-method vocabulary GET, HEAD, and POST. A wrong generalization would extrapolate from newer HTTP versions and accept later methods such as PATCH or arbitrary uppercase tokens.

neighbors.relationship: Contains methods standardized after HTTP/1.0 as well as newer registered methods.
Is another HTTP token class, but it is numeric rather than a closed method lexicon.

row.description: A dotenv file is conventionally a repeated sequence of NAME=value assignments, one assignment per line. This restricted deployment profile uses uppercase environment names and unquoted simple values. A wrong generalization would model the file as one assignment only, or treat repeated lines as a free-form paragraph.

neighbors.relationship: Can use similar NAME=value syntax but has shell expansion and quoting semantics.
Uses repeated key-value entries but commonly groups them into named sections.

positives:
HOST=localhost
PORT=8080
API=enabled
LOG=debug
CACHE=redis_01
WORKER=worker2

row.description: Git accepts a unique hexadecimal object-name prefix; command output often shows seven or twelve characters, but the abbreviation width is variable and may need to grow to remain unique. A wrong generalization would freeze the apparent sample width at seven characters or require a full 40-character SHA-1.

neighbors.relationship: Uses the complete 40-character hexadecimal object name.
May append tag, distance, and dirty-state information around an abbreviated object ID.

concept: Federal district court CM/ECF civil docket number

row.concept: Federal district court CM/ECF civil docket number
row.description: A federal civil-case identifier in the common division:year-cv-sequence presentation used by district-court docket systems.
row.wrong_generalization: Treating every federal docket number as a fixed-width national identifier would wrongly reject courts that omit leading zeroes or use different division and case-type conventions.

concept: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure rule number

row.concept: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure rule number
row.description: The numbered-rule component of a citation to the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

neighbors.concept: Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure rule number

row.wrong_generalization: Using the smallest and largest rule numbers merely observed in a sample would be wrong; the 1–86 window comes from the numbered federal civil-rule set, not sample statistics.

row.description: The concise pleading-title designation used to identify an original complaint or an amended complaint.
row.wrong_generalization: Treating the optional amendment mark as a general revision field would incorrectly accept ordinal amendments such as 'Second Am. Compl.', which require a different caption convention.

concept: SEC EDGAR amended annual-report form type

row.concept: SEC EDGAR amended annual-report form type
row.description: SEC EDGAR form types identify an annual report as "10-K" and append the optional revision marker "/A" when the filing is an amendment.

neighbors.difference: 10-Q is the quarterly-report form type; its amended form is 10-Q/A.
8-K reports current events and has a different filing purpose and structure.

row.wrong_generalization: Assuming every annual report is amended, or allowing an arbitrary slash suffix, loses the specific optional EDGAR amendment convention.

row.description: The FIX Protocol Parties component starts with NoPartyIDs (tag 453) and then repeats PartyID, PartyIDSource, and PartyRole fields for each named party. This simplified structural form uses BIC-like PartyID values and visible pipe delimiters.

neighbors.difference: Instrument identifies the traded security rather than counterparties or executing parties.
SWIFT FIN fields use colon-tagged message fields, not FIX tag-value repeating groups.

row.wrong_generalization: Flattening all FIX tags into one unordered map would discard repeated party instances; production validation must also verify that tag 453 matches the number of repeated groups.

row.description: Clinical laboratory reference interval convention for fasting plasma glucose, reported as a lower and upper reference boundary in mg/dL.

neighbors.relation: single patient result interpreted against the interval
another laboratory reference interval with a different analyte and unit

row.wrong_generalization: The two numbers are not the minimum and maximum values observed in a dataset; they are a clinically defined reference interval. Treating them as sample extrema changes their meaning.

row.description: HL7 Version 2 field repetition convention: repeated field values are separated by the default repetition separator, tilde (~), as in an OBX or PID field when local content is simple coded text.

neighbors.relation: caret separates components within one field repetition
ampersand separates subcomponents within a component

row.wrong_generalization: Treating tilde-separated content as one opaque value is wrong: in HL7 v2, each tilde begins another repetition. Conversely, a trailing or doubled tilde does not represent a populated coded repetition here.

concept: FDA National Drug Code package-label display

row.concept: FDA National Drug Code package-label display
row.description: FDA National Drug Code (NDC) 10-digit display convention, whose hyphenated labeler-product-package segments can be 4-4-2, 5-3-2, or 5-4-1.

neighbors.relation: zero-padded billing normalization of an NDC
drug terminology identifier rather than a package-label code

row.wrong_generalization: Examples can make NDC labels look fixed-width, especially in 4-4-2 form, but FDA 10-digit display layouts vary by segment. Assuming one hyphen position pattern rejects valid NDCs.

row.description: A release artifact filename ending in a recognized file extension.
A copied order-side value from an execution or trade blotter.
A copied U.S.C. citation whose parenthetical subsection may be omitted.
Clinical service date recorded with an uppercase abbreviated month token.
A pallet handling marker consisting of an H prefix and a variable run of X characters.
A lowercase sort-zone label with a numeric aisle and an A through F subzone suffix.
Phase designation copied from a panel or substation drawing.
Ticket number prefixed by an approved sales channel.
Copied PBX extension that may include an optional dial terminator.
A copied academic-term label combining a spring or fall term code with a four-digit year.
A legacy HTTP/1.0 response status field as printed by an HTTP diagnostic or proxy log.
Meaning: an internal nostro reconciliation reference combining a treasury desk prefix, a four-digit control number, and the settlement currency.
Shows the count of authorized rework cycles as repeated R marks on a traveler or inspection tag.
Lists one to three concatenated cadastral block tokens in a land registry system.
Captures a zone designation limited to the eight letters assigned by an agency routing convention.
Stores a lowercase internal handle used to retrieve an agency records folder.
A printed control identifier for routing a document through an internal records queue.
A catalog course code containing an uppercase discipline abbreviation, an optional printed hyphen, and a three-digit course number.
Nine-character uppercase alphanumeric identifier used in a security master.
Alphabetic suffix in a case-file reference; the field permits any uppercase letters even though observed examples use only A-F.
Statutory section citation whose parenthesized lowercase subsection is permitted but optional, despite every sample containing it.
Uppercase chamber code in a court-routing label; the legal field allows any two uppercase letters although samples use A-F only.

ambiguity_types: sampled width is constant although the field permits an open length up to 128
row.description: Lowercase free-text tag used to classify a clinical note.
Carrier tracking reference composed of digits. The field allows open-ended identifier widths, while the sample happens to contain eight-digit values.
Numeric machine serial number field with an open permitted width up to 128 digits, while observed records all use eight digits.
Repeated marker character on a conductor-bundle label; examples do not reach the allowed maximum repetition count.
Mass-unit token attached to fuel shipment quantities; observed tokens form only a small subset of the recognized unit lexicon.
An irrigation schedule code begins with IRR- and contains one to eight repeated wet-cycle marks; the sample never reaches the operational maximum.
A seed batch identifier has an optional -ORGANIC certification suffix; every observed example includes that suffix, even though uncertified batches omit it.
A lot marker with one through eight repeated X characters after its retail lot prefix.
A three-letter SKU that may carry an optional refurbished-item suffix.
Two-letter uppercase network-element region code.
Uppercase radio-bearer token with an open permitted length.
Acknowledgement marker repeated once through eight times in a signalling test burst.
Two-letter radio access mode label with an optional 5G technology suffix.
Two-letter government district identifier intended to allow any uppercase A-Z letters, although observed examples use only A-F.
Uppercase filing token whose field specification permits a long open-ended identifier, although the sample uses four-character values.
Four-digit year recorded for an ordinance, intended to use the conventional 1900-2099 administrative record window rather than only the observed decade.
Map-grid row label with a GRID- prefix followed by one through eight uppercase row-section letters; observed records do not reach the allowed maximum.
FOIA designation whose -APPEAL suffix is optional in the field specification, even though the observed sample includes the suffix.
Fiscal-year string for a government report, intended to allow the established 2000-2099 reporting range although examples fall in the 2020s.
Ballot referendum position field restricted to the two official response labels FOR and AGAINST.
A two-letter laboratory batch prefix recorded as unrestricted uppercase alphabetic characters, although observed prefixes use only A-F.
An instrument run annotation beginning with RUN- followed by an uppercase label that may be long in the field, although observed labels have five letters.
A concentration reporting-unit field that permits mg alone or mg/L, although every observed value includes the optional per-litre suffix.
A scientific tabular-export extension that may be csv or tsv, although the observed export sample contains only csv files.
An approval marker field beginning with TAG- followed by one through eight repeated A markers; the sample does not reach the permitted maximum.
A four-letter uppercase filename stem with an optional .pdf suffix; the available examples include the suffix even though it is optional in the field.
A numeric archive-box identifier after BOX- with one through eight digit positions; the observed identifiers never use the allowed maximum width.
An International Registration Data Identifier used to identify standardized product-data dictionary concepts in IEC 61360 and related industrial classification systems.

neighbors.description: A related identifier whose registry body may use another registered prefix.
A product-classification identifier that commonly uses the same IRDI family of syntax.

row.wrong_generalization: Treating the hyphens and number signs as decorative punctuation would wrongly accept reordered segments, omitted separators, or arbitrary UUID-like identifiers.

row.description: A STEP physical-file entity instance reference consisting of a number sign followed by a positive integer, used to link CAD and product-model entities.

neighbors.description: The named EXPRESS entity type following an instance name in a STEP physical file.
A positional value inside an aggregate, not a globally referable entity instance name.

row.wrong_generalization: Three-digit samples can look fixed-width, but STEP instance numbers are variable-width positive integers; padding them or limiting them to three digits would reject valid large models.

row.description: Real convention: IEC 60076 vector-group notation identifies winding connections and the phase-displacement clock number, such as Dyn11 or Yy0. Wrong generalization: assuming the clock number is always two characters because common examples end in 11 would reject valid one-digit clock numbers such as 0 or 5.

neighbors.distinction: Expresses impedance data rather than winding connection and phase displacement.
May resemble a compact mixed-case engineering identifier but does not use transformer clock-hour semantics.

row.description: AAPFCO-style fertilizer package labeling declares a net quantity using a numeric mass followed by a recognized mass unit.

neighbors.relation: same_product_label
related_measurement

ambiguity_types: numeric value range versus observed sample range
row.description: GS1 AI 3902 represents an amount payable with two implied decimal places; its numeric field may contain from 1 through 15 digits.

neighbors.concept: GS1 amount payable with three implied decimals
neighbors.description: Uses a different application identifier and decimal interpretation.
Usually displays an explicit currency symbol and decimal separator.

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization would infer a six-digit amount because the examples happen to be short, rather than preserving the actual 1-to-15-digit numeric window and the fixed two-decimal implied scale.

row.description: Retail delivery advice messages use repeating LIN line-item segments; each segment carries a line number and an item identifier qualifier.

neighbors.description: Represents ordered items rather than dispatched items.
Represents checkout transactions rather than supplier delivery advice.

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization would parse only one LIN segment, omit the segment terminator, or accept a different identifier qualifier as equivalent to the retail GTIN qualifier EN.

row.description: 3GPP PLMN display notation uses a three-digit Mobile Country Code and a two- or three-digit Mobile Network Code separated by a literal hyphen, as in 310-260. A wrong generalization would remove the hyphen because database forms often concatenate MCC and MNC, thereby accepting an unformatted identifier where this presentation convention requires the separator.

neighbors.relationship: A subscriber number may be served by a PLMN but does not encode MCC-MNC in this hyphenated form.
An IMSI begins with MCC and MNC but continues with a subscriber identity and is not written as a standalone PLMN code.

row.description: RFC 3261 SIP URI syntax permits a repeated semicolon-prefixed URI-parameter section after the host, for example transport and user parameters. A wrong generalization would model only one parameter because examples often show a single suffix, rejecting valid URIs with multiple parameter sections.

neighbors.relationship: A tel URI identifies a telephone number and uses different parameter rules from a SIP URI.
A Contact header may contain a SIP URI but additionally has header-level display-name and parameter syntax.

row.description: ITU-T E.164 international-number notation uses a leading plus sign followed by up to 15 digits. Samples from one national numbering plan can appear to have a fixed width, but E.164 is variable-width across country codes and national significant numbers. A wrong generalization would hard-code the apparent sample length, such as 11 digits, and reject valid shorter or longer international numbers.

neighbors.relationship: A national significant number is interpreted within a numbering plan and normally omits the E.164 plus form.
An IMSI is a mobile subscriber identity that can begin with country and network codes but is not an E.164 dialable number.

row.description: The U.S. Standard Form 424 naming convention may append an optional parenthesized revision month and year, such as SF-424 (Rev. 12/2022).

neighbors.distinction: Identifies an information-collection approval, commonly in a 1234-5678 pattern.
Names a related budget-information form rather than a revision of SF-424.

row.wrong_generalization: Requiring a revision mark because every sampled PDF happens to show one would reject valid base form labels; allowing arbitrary parenthetical prose would lose the controlled revision-date structure.

row.convention: HGVS sequence-variant nomenclature for cis-listed cDNA substitutions
row.description: A bracketed HGVS cDNA allele expression can contain one substitution followed by repeated semicolon-separated substitutions on the same allele.

neighbors.relation: uses g. rather than c. coordinates
uses p. amino-acid notation

row.wrong_generalization: Flattening the bracketed expression into an unrestricted delimiter-separated string loses the allele grouping and incorrectly permits commas, dangling separators, or an unbracketed multi-variant list.

row.description: ISBN-13 is the book-identification convention defined by ISO 2108. This profile uses the visible 3-1-4-4-1 hyphenation layout. A wrong generalization would treat hyphens as optional decoration or accept any 13-digit number without validating the ISBN-13 check digit and registration-group structure.

neighbors.distinction: ISSN identifies serial publications and has eight digits rather than the ISBN-13 book identifier layout.
A DOI is a resolver-oriented identifier with slash-separated registrant syntax rather than an ISBN registration-group pattern.

concept: ASME drawing number with optional revision suffix

row.concept: ASME drawing number with optional revision suffix
row.description: Technical-drawing control commonly uses an ASME Y14.100-style drawing identifier with a revision letter for a revised issue; an initial issue may omit the revision suffix. A wrong generalization would require a revision for every drawing, accept numeric revision marks in a letter-only workflow, or treat the revision as part of the immutable drawing number.

neighbors.distinction: An issue date records publication time, whereas the revision suffix identifies a controlled revision state.
An ECO authorizes a change; it is not the revision identifier printed on the drawing.

row.description: PDF print and export dialogs conventionally express selected page intervals as comma-separated inclusive ranges, for example 1-3,5-7. A wrong generalization would treat the field as unrestricted prose, allow a bare page number when this range-only profile is expected, or accept typographic dashes that a machine parser does not recognize as range separators.

neighbors.distinction: A single page reference names one page, while this profile requires explicit start-end range sections.
A bookmark destination is a navigational target rather than a print-selection interval list.

row.description: A classic PDF cross-reference-table entry stores its byte offset as a zero-padded decimal field with exactly ten digits before the generation-number field. The apparent fixed width in samples is normative for the classic xref-table syntax, not evidence that offsets are ordinary variable-width integers. A wrong generalization would strip leading zeros or accept shorter offsets without padding.

neighbors.distinction: The generation number is a bounded object-version counter, while this field is a byte position in the PDF file.
A stream length is ordinarily represented as an integer object and is not constrained to the classic xref ten-character field width.

row.description: The commercial AWS partition convention for naming an S3 bucket resource is arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name. S3 bucket ARNs deliberately leave the region and account components empty.

neighbors.relation: same ARN family, but account is mandatory
same service, but includes region and account

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to require every AWS ARN to contain nonempty region and account fields. S3 bucket ARNs use the same colon-separated ARN shape but intentionally leave both fields blank.

row.description: An API Gateway route method is an IANA-registered HTTP method token, such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, CONNECT, or TRACE.

neighbors.relation: paired with a method to form an API route
another HTTP-layer field but numeric rather than lexical

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to accept any uppercase alphabetic token as an HTTP method. Route configuration should use the IANA HTTP-method vocabulary rather than treating arbitrary verbs as valid methods.

row.description: S3 object keys are flat strings, but console and tooling conventions use slash-terminated repeated segments as a folder-style prefix, for example logs/2025/.

neighbors.relation: the complete flat key that may begin with this prefix
similar visual notation but different hierarchy semantics

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to treat S3 prefixes as actual filesystem directories. The slash is part of the object-key string; the repeated slash-terminated form is a useful listing convention, not a server-enforced directory hierarchy.

row.description: Course learning outcomes are often tagged as CLO-1, CLO-2, and so on; catalog and accreditation exports may serialize multiple tags as a semicolon-delimited list. The repeated section represents multiple outcome references, not a single compound outcome number. A wrong generalization is to accept comma-separated prose or to assume only one CLO tag can occur.

neighbors.relation: program-level outcome rather than course-level outcome
measurement criterion rather than stated learning outcome

row.wrong_generalization: A learning-outcome field contains one unrestricted number, or semicolons can be replaced by arbitrary punctuation.

row.description: The California Statewide Student Identifier (SSID) is represented as a ten-digit student identifier in statewide K-12 data exchanges. Its width is fixed even when samples happen to resemble ordinary integers. A wrong generalization is to strip leading zeroes, permit shorter local student numbers, or infer that any ten-digit number is an issued SSID.

neighbors.relation: institution-assigned identifier with local formatting rules
different postsecondary identity and reporting context

row.wrong_generalization: The field is a variable-width integer, so leading zeroes may be removed and any ten-digit number is valid.

row.convention: CMS Medicare Beneficiary Identifier hyphenated display convention
row.description: The Medicare Beneficiary Identifier (MBI) is commonly displayed as three groups separated by hyphens, such as 1EG4-TE5-MK73, for Medicare insurance eligibility and claims administration.

neighbors.distinction: The older HICN convention can contain a claim-account suffix and is not an MBI.
An NPI is a 10-digit provider identifier rather than a beneficiary identifier.

row.wrong_generalization: Treating the hyphens as optional because some system-to-system payloads omit display punctuation, or assuming every 11-character insurance identifier is an MBI.

row.description: Certificates of Liability Insurance identify the ACORD 25 form and may include an optional parenthesized edition revision, for example ACORD 25 (2016/03).

neighbors.distinction: The issue date identifies when a particular certificate was produced.
The effective date begins policy coverage and is unrelated to the ACORD form edition.

row.wrong_generalization: Requiring an edition mark on every certificate, or treating the edition date as the certificate issuance date.

row.convention: ANSI X12 835 Claim Adjustment Segment (CAS) convention
row.description: In an ANSI X12 835 remittance advice, a CAS segment carries an adjustment group code followed by one or more repeated claim-adjustment reason, amount, and quantity sections.

neighbors.distinction: CLP communicates claim-level payment information rather than adjustment reasons.
An 837 claim may carry CAS information, but its transaction context and usage differ from an 835 remittance.

row.wrong_generalization: Assuming a CAS segment contains only one adjustment, or parsing repeated adjustment triples as independent segments.

row.description: A claim reference number is carrier-assigned and is commonly recorded on loss notices, claim correspondence, and policy servicing systems. Samples often appear to have one fixed width even though insurers use varying internal lengths.

neighbors.distinction: A policy number identifies a contract or policy term rather than a reported loss.
A claimant identifier identifies a person or organization associated with the claim, not the claim file itself.

row.wrong_generalization: Inferring a fixed ten-digit width from a sample file, or assuming a numeric claim reference can be validated without the issuing carrier's system.

row.description: Real convention: IEC 60076 vector-group notation identifies winding connections and the phase-displacement clock number, such as Dyn11 or Yy0. Wrong generalization: assuming the clock number is always two characters because common examples end in 11 would reject valid one-digit clock numbers such as 0 or 5.

neighbors.distinction: Expresses impedance data rather than winding connection and phase displacement.
May resemble a compact mixed-case engineering identifier but does not use transformer clock-hour semantics.

row.description: AAPFCO-style fertilizer package labeling declares a net quantity using a numeric mass followed by a recognized mass unit.

neighbors.relation: same_product_label
related_measurement

ambiguity_types: numeric value range versus observed sample range
row.description: GS1 AI 3902 represents an amount payable with two implied decimal places; its numeric field may contain from 1 through 15 digits.

neighbors.concept: GS1 amount payable with three implied decimals
neighbors.description: Uses a different application identifier and decimal interpretation.
Usually displays an explicit currency symbol and decimal separator.

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization would infer a six-digit amount because the examples happen to be short, rather than preserving the actual 1-to-15-digit numeric window and the fixed two-decimal implied scale.

row.description: Retail delivery advice messages use repeating LIN line-item segments; each segment carries a line number and an item identifier qualifier.

neighbors.description: Represents ordered items rather than dispatched items.
Represents checkout transactions rather than supplier delivery advice.

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization would parse only one LIN segment, omit the segment terminator, or accept a different identifier qualifier as equivalent to the retail GTIN qualifier EN.

row.description: RFC 3261 SIP URI syntax permits a repeated semicolon-prefixed URI-parameter section after the host, for example transport and user parameters. A wrong generalization would model only one parameter because examples often show a single suffix, rejecting valid URIs with multiple parameter sections.

neighbors.relationship: A tel URI identifies a telephone number and uses different parameter rules from a SIP URI.
A Contact header may contain a SIP URI but additionally has header-level display-name and parameter syntax.

row.description: The U.S. Standard Form 424 naming convention may append an optional parenthesized revision month and year, such as SF-424 (Rev. 12/2022).

neighbors.distinction: Identifies an information-collection approval, commonly in a 1234-5678 pattern.
Names a related budget-information form rather than a revision of SF-424.

row.wrong_generalization: Requiring a revision mark because every sampled PDF happens to show one would reject valid base form labels; allowing arbitrary parenthetical prose would lose the controlled revision-date structure.

row.convention: HGVS sequence-variant nomenclature for cis-listed cDNA substitutions
row.description: A bracketed HGVS cDNA allele expression can contain one substitution followed by repeated semicolon-separated substitutions on the same allele.

neighbors.relation: uses g. rather than c. coordinates
uses p. amino-acid notation

row.wrong_generalization: Flattening the bracketed expression into an unrestricted delimiter-separated string loses the allele grouping and incorrectly permits commas, dangling separators, or an unbracketed multi-variant list.

row.description: ISBN-13 is the book-identification convention defined by ISO 2108. This profile uses the visible 3-1-4-4-1 hyphenation layout. A wrong generalization would treat hyphens as optional decoration or accept any 13-digit number without validating the ISBN-13 check digit and registration-group structure.

neighbors.distinction: ISSN identifies serial publications and has eight digits rather than the ISBN-13 book identifier layout.
A DOI is a resolver-oriented identifier with slash-separated registrant syntax rather than an ISBN registration-group pattern.

row.description: PDF print and export dialogs conventionally express selected page intervals as comma-separated inclusive ranges, for example 1-3,5-7. A wrong generalization would treat the field as unrestricted prose, allow a bare page number when this range-only profile is expected, or accept typographic dashes that a machine parser does not recognize as range separators.

neighbors.distinction: A single page reference names one page, while this profile requires explicit start-end range sections.
A bookmark destination is a navigational target rather than a print-selection interval list.

row.description: The commercial AWS partition convention for naming an S3 bucket resource is arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name. S3 bucket ARNs deliberately leave the region and account components empty.

neighbors.relation: same ARN family, but account is mandatory
same service, but includes region and account

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to require every AWS ARN to contain nonempty region and account fields. S3 bucket ARNs use the same colon-separated ARN shape but intentionally leave both fields blank.

row.description: An API Gateway route method is an IANA-registered HTTP method token, such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, CONNECT, or TRACE.

neighbors.relation: paired with a method to form an API route
another HTTP-layer field but numeric rather than lexical

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to accept any uppercase alphabetic token as an HTTP method. Route configuration should use the IANA HTTP-method vocabulary rather than treating arbitrary verbs as valid methods.

row.description: S3 object keys are flat strings, but console and tooling conventions use slash-terminated repeated segments as a folder-style prefix, for example logs/2025/.

neighbors.relation: the complete flat key that may begin with this prefix
similar visual notation but different hierarchy semantics

row.wrong_generalization: A wrong generalization is to treat S3 prefixes as actual filesystem directories. The slash is part of the object-key string; the repeated slash-terminated form is a useful listing convention, not a server-enforced directory hierarchy.

row.description: Course learning outcomes are often tagged as CLO-1, CLO-2, and so on; catalog and accreditation exports may serialize multiple tags as a semicolon-delimited list. The repeated section represents multiple outcome references, not a single compound outcome number. A wrong generalization is to accept comma-separated prose or to assume only one CLO tag can occur.

neighbors.relation: program-level outcome rather than course-level outcome
measurement criterion rather than stated learning outcome

row.wrong_generalization: A learning-outcome field contains one unrestricted number, or semicolons can be replaced by arbitrary punctuation.

row.description: The California Statewide Student Identifier (SSID) is represented as a ten-digit student identifier in statewide K-12 data exchanges. Its width is fixed even when samples happen to resemble ordinary integers. A wrong generalization is to strip leading zeroes, permit shorter local student numbers, or infer that any ten-digit number is an issued SSID.

neighbors.relation: institution-assigned identifier with local formatting rules
different postsecondary identity and reporting context

row.wrong_generalization: The field is a variable-width integer, so leading zeroes may be removed and any ten-digit number is valid.

row.convention: CMS Medicare Beneficiary Identifier hyphenated display convention
row.description: The Medicare Beneficiary Identifier (MBI) is commonly displayed as three groups separated by hyphens, such as 1EG4-TE5-MK73, for Medicare insurance eligibility and claims administration.

neighbors.distinction: The older HICN convention can contain a claim-account suffix and is not an MBI.
An NPI is a 10-digit provider identifier rather than a beneficiary identifier.

row.wrong_generalization: Treating the hyphens as optional because some system-to-system payloads omit display punctuation, or assuming every 11-character insurance identifier is an MBI.

row.description: Certificates of Liability Insurance identify the ACORD 25 form and may include an optional parenthesized edition revision, for example ACORD 25 (2016/03).

neighbors.distinction: The issue date identifies when a particular certificate was produced.
The effective date begins policy coverage and is unrelated to the ACORD form edition.

row.wrong_generalization: Requiring an edition mark on every certificate, or treating the edition date as the certificate issuance date.
